name: How to Spot an Underbid Remodeling Quote

mainEntity.name: What are the biggest red flags that a contractor may underbid my remodel on purpose?
mainEntity.text: What are the biggest red flags that a contractor may underbid my remodel on purpose?

acceptedAnswer.text: An underbid often shows up as a quote that looks great on the total line but lacks detail. Common red flags include missing permit costs, low allowances for finishes, unclear scope descriptions, no mention of site protection or cleanup, and vague language about exclusions. Another warning sign is when a contractor avoids discussing how change orders are handled or refuses to itemize major components. In ADU and remodel work, a low bid can lead to cost creep once the job begins and reality forces pricing adjustments. Homeowners should ask for a line-by-line breakdown and compare all bids using the same scope assumptions. A well-prepared contractor should be able to explain why a bid is priced the way it is and where potential risks may occur.
acceptedAnswer.description: Red flags include vague scope, unusually low allowances, missing permit language, no clear timeline, weak change-order terms, and reluctance to specify materials or labor details. An underbid may look attractive at first but can lead to aggressive change orders later. Comparing line items is the best way to catch this early.
